mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—let’s take a moment to imagine what really goes on beneath the calm surface of our everyday digital lives. Every search you make, every post you like, every late-night question you type into a search engine—these quiet moments build up into something huge. While we all wear social masks and keep up appearances, there’s one place where honesty slips through the cracks: those anonymous corners of the internet. That’s the world Seth Stephens-Davidowitz explores in his eye-opening book, Everybody Lies: Big Data, New Data, and What the Internet Can Tell Us About Who We Really Are. He invites us to peek behind the digital curtain, where our search histories and online habits reveal our real thoughts, dreams, and even fears—stuff we’d never dare say out loud. As we sift through billions of digital footprints, surprising patterns start to appear. We’re faced with unexpected truths about honesty, prejudice, even happiness—shining a light on how people really act when no one’s watching. The gap between our public selves and private realities? It’s wider than you might think. Together, we’ll uncover how this flood of new data is changing what we know about politics, relationships, the economy, and how we see ourselves. The journey ahead is full of revelations—and more than a few ethical questions—about what happens when big data turns into a window straight into the human soul. So, are you ready to see what lies beneath the surface? Let’s dive in.
